Certified Healthcare Safety Professional (CHSP), Certified Healthcare Facility Manager (CHFM), Certified Safety Professional (CSP) and/or Certified Health Care Environmental Services Professional (CHESP) (Preferred)
Bachelor’s degree in Safety Management, Healthcare Administration, Facilities Management, or related field. (Preferred)

2+ years of hands-on experience and/or ability to learn managing or coordinating Environment of Care, occupational health and safety, or facilities safety programs in an outpatient clinic, student health center, or ambulatory healthcare setting.

Direct experience preparing for, participating in, or leading and/or ability to learn accreditation surveys and compliance audits (specifically AAAHC, The Joint Commission, or equivalent ambulatory care bodies).
Minimum 2 years of experience in healthcare safety, environment of care, or facilities management. (Required)

UHS’ Environment of Care is the physical and organizational setting where healthcare is provided.  The goal of Environment of Care (EOC) is to create a safe and supportive environment that minimizes risks and promotes quality healthcare. The Environment of Care (EOC) Officer serves as the central organizational connector and coordinator responsible for the EOC Program. The role provides centralized coordination, accountability, risk identification, follow-through, documentation, and communication across internal departments and campus partners to ensure a safe, secure, functional, and compliant healthcare environment. The EOC Officer oversees physical structure, safety protocols, hazardous materials, emergency preparedness, medical equipment, security, utility systems, and staff training related to Environment of Care.
Environment of Care (EOC) Compliance and Program Management - 40%

The EOC Officer is responsible for the EOC Program which includes developing, implementing, and managing programs and policies that ensure a safe, functional, and compliant healthcare environment for patients, staff, and visitors.  It involves ongoing monitoring, assessment, and improvement to ensure compliance with regulations and standards, as well as to provide a positive experience for all stakeholders. The EOC Officer’s duties include physical structure (building design, layout, accessibility, fire safety, emergency preparedness), equipment and supplies (medical devices, infection control, waste management), EOC policies (development, ownership, review), security (access control, surveillance, incident response), business continuity planning, and staff training (safety protocols, emergency response, infection control).

Develops and maintains the EOC program. Ensure compliance with American Association for Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC), University of California Office of the President, University of California Berkeley and state/local regulations and/or the ability to learn.

Lead the Health, Safety and Security Committee; prepare meeting agendas, minutes, and reports. Ensure adherence to fire safety, hazardous materials handling, infection prevention, and emergency preparedness protocols.

Collaborate with Facilities, Security, and Occupational Health departments to address environmental concerns. Maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation related to safety inspections, incident reports, and emergency drills.
Coordinates programs to prevent injury and identify/correct environmental hazards. Oversees accident, injury, and fall reporting and trending.
Conducts structured, recurring Environment of Care rounds and hazard surveillance across UHS locations. Tracks incident investigations and corrective actions, partnering closely with Risk Management.

Hazardous Materials & Waste Management: Oversees the safe handling, storage, inventory, and disposal of chemicals, biological hazards, regulated medical waste, and pharmaceutical waste. Coordinates chemical inventory/SDS maintenance, spill and exposure response protocols, vendor services, and staff training compliance.
Emergency Preparedness - 20%
Maintains an all-hazards approach for UHS emergency management planning. Oversee annual hazard assessments. Ensures compliance with accreditation standards of performance.

Coordinate and oversee quarterly drills, including planned exercises and real-life events. Provide after action reports for drills or events for all UHS locations (Tang, Anna Head, Haas Pavilion, Simpson Center).
Represent UHS at campus or committee emergency management meetings. Develop and maintain emergency preparedness plans and procedures.
Maintain emergency management and UCB business continuity plans and ensure clinic and department readiness and/or the ability to learn.
Coordinates fire safety rounds, evacuation drills, egress maintenance, and staff life-safety education.
Coordinates with Facilities and the campus Fire Marshal for fire alarm/sprinkler/extinguisher inspections, construction/remodel reviews, and corrective action tracking.
Policy and Procedure Implementation and Maintenance - 10%
Assist with the development, implementation, and updates of Environment of Care policies and procedures.
Ensure EOC policies are consistently applied across departments.
Chairs the Environment of Care multi departmental committee.
Inspections, Audits and Risk Assessments, Data Collection and Reporting - 10%
Conduct regular environment of care rounds and hazard surveillance (e.g., hazard vulnerability analysis and hazard safety assessment), documenting findings and ensuring timely corrective actions.
Maintain logs and records for safety, incidents, inspections, and drills.
Prepare regular reports for leadership and regulatory agencies. Track and report safety trends and deficiencies to leadership.
Prepare and present an annual EOC report to the Risk and Quality Committee.
Training, Education and Other Duties as Assigned - 10%
Develops and delivers EOC-related education and training programs for staff.

Ensure staff training on and completion of safety topics including at a minimum fire extinguisher use, hazardous waste handling, evacuation procedures, bloodborne pathogen standards, and emergency response protocols.
Other duties as assigned.
Equipment and Facilities - 10%
Ensure medical and non-medical equipment is maintained, tested, and inspected per required schedules.
Work with business operations facilities/maintenance teams to resolve physical environment concerns (e.g., lighting, temperature, signage, exits).
Track the status of EOC-related repair work orders and ensure timely resolution of identified issues.
Advise on capital projects from an EOC perspective. Advise or help oversee purchases from an EOC perspective.
Working knowledge of healthcare environmental safety regulations, standards, and practices (e.g., AAAHC, OSHA, Cal/OSHA, local fire codes, and life safety regulations).

Familiarity with and/or ability to learn higher education administrative structures, campus safety protocols, campus Fire Marshal procedures, and University of California policies or similar institutional frameworks.

Demonstrated ability to support or coordinate all-hazards emergency planning, hazard vulnerability assessments, business continuity plans, and emergency drills (e.g., fire, evacuation, emergency response). Ability to respond effectively in emergencies.

Basic-to-intermediate knowledge of compliance standards for handling, inventorying, and disposing of regulated medical waste, pharmaceutical waste, chemical hazards, and bloodborne pathogen protocols.
Ability to conduct structured hazard surveillance, safety inspections, and environment of care rounds, with demonstrated skill in identifying hazards and tracking corrective actions to resolution.

Demonstrated ability to collaborate with facilities maintenance, physical plant teams, and external inspectors/vendors to track work orders, verify equipment maintenance schedules, and address physical environment concerns.
Strong critical thinking skills to investigate safety incidents, analyze risk findings and trend data, and formulate practical, compliant corrective action plans.

Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to develop and deliver mandatory safety training programs, present clear reports to leadership committees, and lead multi-departmental committee meetings.

Strong organizational skills with high attention to detail, capable of maintaining precise regulatory logs, incident reports, policy documentation, and inspection records across multiple healthcare sites.
